#2060. AC Milan 3-1 Inter: Five things we learned – individual and tactical success

AC Milan clinched a massive victory in their home derby against Inter on Saturday, with several positives to take from the game as a result.

There wasn’t exactly an excess of optimism before the game among the Milan fans, following what was a poor mid-week defeat and a so-so start to the season. However, we didn’t see much of this in the big game, with two goals scored after just ten minutes.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s almost as if Gerry Cardinale manifested the win before the game and he certainly got to celebrate afterwards, even brought to tears in the mixed zone. He probably learnt a lot from this game and so did we, with several positives to highlight.

Without Diego Moreira, Adrien Rabiot and Mario Gila, Milan and Ruben Amorim struggled a lot in the mid-week clash against Bologna. Fortunately, the trio was back against Inter and the difference was clear as night and day.

All three played a big role, but the true difference-maker was Moreira, who was elctric from the start after bagging an early and lovely assist for Christian Pulisic. Six minutes later, in the 10th minute, he picked up a second from a corner kick, setting up Rabiot.

Inter got back into the game a little with their goal, making it 2-1, and it was a delicate moment in the game when Milan needed to stay focused. And yet again, it was Moreira who brought them out of trouble with a fantastic free-kick just before half-time.

San Siro erupted and the Belgian certainly showed that he has several tricks up his sleeve. On top of the attacking contribution, the Belgian was relentless throughout the game as he helped a tonne defensively until the final whistle.

Milan seem to have a game changer in their hands and it was fitting that he delivered this type of performance in his first Derby Della Madonnina. Especially since Ricky Kaka was in the stands, the player who made Moreira choose the No.22 shirt.

Milan did an outstanding job up front, being as clinical as they could be, but Inter were always going to create chances on the other end. So, it was even more impressive how the Rossoneri managed to contain them, especially in the second half.

There were some struggling moments in the first half, but in that period, Mike Maignan came up big with multiple good saves. One of them was just phenomenal, as he had little to no time to react and it was all about the Frenchman’s reflexes, which didn’t let him down.

That was a crucial moment in the game, with the result being 2-1 for Milan and with an equaliser there, the game could’ve been a lot different.

In the second half, the Rossoneri were a lot more compact and it was more about the players in front of Maignan. Strahinja Pavlovic stepped up a tonne after the half-time mark as he was a tad shaky in the opening 45 minutes, especially against Spence who was bursting down that flank.

Gila was also very solid on the right-hand side and especially when he was on the ball. It’s a completely different team when he’s on the pitch.

Diawara, Musah and Modric also did a very fine job closing down the spaces and handling Inter’s press well, with the Croatian rolling the years back as he was relentless throughout the game.

It was a very impressive defensive performance and especially in the second half of the game, as it seems Amorim’s instructions at the break limited Inter even further.

I purposefully left out Koni De Winter from the previous point because I think the Belgian deserves a section all for himself.

In the absence of Lautaro, Thuram was always going to be the main threat. Not just because he has five goals and four assists in the opening eight games, but also because he has done very well in the derby before.

So naturally, if Milan were to win the game, they had to neutralise the Frenchman and it was clear from the beginning that De Winter’s instructions were to stay close to the striker and not give him breathing space.

De Winter deserves all the praise here because he won almost all of the duels against the striker, effectively frustrating him and getting him out of the game completely. The only memory I have from Thuram was when he dropped almost into his own half towards the end of the game to try and make something happen, but that was not nearly enough.

Aside from his battle with the Frenchman, De Winter also did well with his passing and overall game and was arguably the best Milan defender on the night.

Really positive performance and he needs to keep it up, because conceding silly goals has been a problem for Milan and they clearly have the quality to prevent them.

We already mentioned the brilliant work at the back and the saves Maignan made, but it’s only fair to praise the attack too as they also did a fine job. Milan had three shots on goal until the 90th minute and had scored three goals, which is impressive considering how wasteful the Rossoneri have been in attack in the last few games.

The team started off with the right mindset and put pressure on Inter early on, with some great individual runs such as the one from Moreira. All of the chances were finished with clinical precision, which is exactly what you need to win in the big games.

We already praised Moreira, but Pulisic was also very good as he found the empty space on the opener and buried it to give his side the lead. He then continued playing well between the lines and he was smart about controlling the game after his side was ahead.

Rabiot came in clutch again with yet another goal and a positive performance overall, even if he had to do a bit more running in the second half and focus on the defensive aspect of the game.

I know he failed to score or assist again, but that doesn’t mean Goncalo Ramos was necessarily bad. He pressed quite a bit and he opened up spaces for his teammates. You can clearly see on Milan’s second goal how he pushes Sucic towards the byline so he can’t charge towards Rabiot after Moreira’s corner.

Again, he absolutely needs to be more involved in the box but he’s still a very valuable player on the pitch.

There was obviously a bittersweet feeling coming into the derby after losing to Bologna in such a frustrating manner, but the availability of Moreira, Rabiot and Gila gave Amorim and the fans some enthusiasm prior to the game.

To Amorim’s credit, he picked the correct starting eleven and his team had the right mindset from the start. The coach was aware of Inter’s fragile defending and instructed his team to raise the intensity from the start and apply pressure, which worked a treat with two goals in the opening ten minutes.

Inter then tried to come back into the game and created a few chances, it’s fair to say, but Amorim again tweaked something at the half-time break. His team was more compact and more aggressive after that, which almost completely neutralised Inter.

The coach also waited with his subs, which I think was correct given the team was playing well and there weren’t obvious signs of fatigue. When the changes did come, I think they were spot on.

More importantly, the whole game management was impressive. The game started off with Milan playing in Amorim’s style, which resulted in the goals but also exposed his team and then in the second half, Milan were more compact and not eager to press or attack as much.

On top of that, there were numerous times when the Rossoneri kept the ball, were patient and avoided risk and I think the tempo was dictated by Milan despite Inter having a bit more possession towards the end. Excellent from the coach.

#2055. Chelsea news: three positives and two disappointments... verdict on five players sent to Strasbourg

By Axel Clody | 05 Nov 2026 07:02

Very active in the last summer transfer window, Strasbourg signed five players from Chelsea. A few weeks after their arrival in Alsace, what is the verdict on their first steps with the club?

Revived by a home thrashing of Auxerre (5-1) after four consecutive defeats, Strasbourg have had a stop-start opening to the season.

Probably not helped by too big a squad overhaul in the last summer window, with close to £85m (€100m) spent and 17 signings registered, the Alsace club are suffering the full effect of a transfer mistake recently highlighted by Ismael Doukoure: a sizeable quota of foreign players and not a single signing with any Ligue 1 experience.

Among the summer arrivals, Hugo Oliveira’s side signed five players from Chelsea, the club with which Strasbourg share the same owner, BlueCo, in a collaboration designed to make transactions between the two sides easier.

They are Brazilian forward Deivid Washington, who cost £13.6m (€16m), English attacking midfielder Omari Kellyman, who cost £5.1m (€6m), Danish goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen on loan, Portuguese defensive midfielder Dario Essugo on loan and Swedish right-back Genesis Antwi on loan. Five players with radically different playing time and performances since the start of the 2026-27 season.

A few months after their arrival in France, what verdict can be drawn? Three positives and two disappointments stand out.

On the positive side, Dario Essugo has made four starts in seven appearances, with two goals and one assist. In terms of presence on the pitch, Filip Jorgensen outstrips the competition with nine starts in nine matches and a status strengthened by wearing the captain’s armband in three games. Although he has not yet kept a clean sheet, he has made 32 saves.

Genesis Antwi, for his part, has started eight times, with Hugo Oliveira only leaving him on the bench against Auxerre. The 19-year-old has just been rewarded for his good performances with a first call-up to Graham Potter’s Sweden squad for the upcoming international break and the Nations League matches against Bosnia-Herzegovina and Poland.

For the two other Chelsea recruits, however, the verdict is not very impressive. Deivid Washington, Strasbourg’s second most expensive signing of summer 2026, has so far been a flop: the Brazilian has still not played a single minute.

Finally, Omari Kellyman has only one appearance, for just six minutes, in a 3-0 defeat to Rennes on 25 October. In other words, the pile-up of players in Strasbourg’s squad has not stopped some from standing out while others remain on the sidelines. It is one way of weighing up the pros and cons of the club’s huge summer 2026 recruitment drive.

#2052. GdS: An ‘achievable dream’ – why Cardinale left Italy ‘convinced’ by Scudetto bid

Gerry Cardinale left San Siro after the derby win over Inter with a distinct feeling: this AC Milan team can challenge for the title.

Happy as ever about the derby victory, yet still rueful over the defeat to Bologna – a stumble that must not be repeated – La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) write that Cardinale departed Italy yesterday, bound for New York, where his family and work await him.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

His thoughts however remain firmly fixed on AC Milan and the tasks that lie ahead, with the renewal of Adrien Rabiot’s contract as a short-term priority and the Scudetto as a cherished, long-term dream.

He admitted as much following the loss to Raffaele Palladino’s side, and he feels it even more strongly now, having won his first derby since taking direct personal control of the club on May 25th.

On Sunday evening, following the final whistle, Cardinale chose not to speak to the team. He had already said everything he needed to say to his players on Saturday at Milanello, aiming to motivate and spur them on to bounce back from the 4-2 defeat against Bologna.

The team took his words to heart: after the derby, Maignan and his team-mates could see the joy on Cardinale’s face, even though he didn’t utter a single word. Amorim, who granted the squad two days of (training set to resume tomorrow) offered his own praise for the team’s performance.

The head of RedBird Capital stepped away from the dressing room, wanting the moment to remain special for the players and the coaching staff, but also because he was deeply moved—tears nearly welling up in his eyes.

Milan, its fans, and the project itself all needed a night like this, and the American knew it. Now, however, Gerry expects the level of performance shown in the derby to be replicated in the upcoming matches, specifically the two before the break: Thursday against Ferencváros and Sunday in Genoa.

These are fixtures that will require managing the post-derby euphoria to ensure there is no drop in focus. While some of the squad celebrated at a well-known Milanese nightclub on Saturday night, the focus shifts to Europe starting tomorrow.

The position in the table needs to be improved following the slip-ups against Benfica and Bournemouth in the first three games. Beyond that, further progress will be required in Serie A.

The only way to close the seven-point gap on Lazio is to avoid any further stumbles like the one against Bologna. On this point, Cardinale and Amorim are in complete agreement.

In fact, while both were delighted by the triumph over their city rivals, that joy only sharpened their regret over the three points dropped against the Rossoblù. Neither the manager nor the owner could stomach the collapse from a 2-1 lead at halftime to a 4-2 defeat.

The two spoke after the derby and are fully aligned: injuries notwithstanding, a Milan side that aspires to be Milan once again – both in Italy and in Europe – cannot afford such lapses in focus.

Beating Inter is satisfying, and remaining unbeaten against their rivals for eight consecutive matches is a positive, but the ultimate priority remains lifting a trophy. City supremacy is not enough, not for Cardinale, and not for Amorim.

King's team-building is remarkable - and it is not random. The manager is - he will not mind the Herald saying it - a football obsessive. He's not the Messiah. But he's a very canny manager, and in a matter of months, he has transformed a football club.

#2049. Barcelona: Raphinha to extend contract until 2030, three factors behind new deal

By Axel Clody | 05 Nov 2026 07:10

There could not be a better time for Raphinha to have his contract renewed by Barcelona. On Thursday, Barcelona will extend the deal of the Brazilian, who is the team’s current captain, until mid-2030, according to Trivela.

As well as being handed the captain’s armband this season, the Brazil international forward is arguably the best player in the world since the competitions began in August. Playing as a centre-forward, he has become a goal machine: 19 in only 13 matches in 2026-27.

It is a revolution the forward has experienced at the Catalan club since 2024. Signed in 2022, he was criticised and even questioned his future at the club, wavering over proposals from Saudi football.

The turning point came with the arrival of Hansi Flick, who convinced him to stay and turned him into one of the best players in the world, first on the left wing. In 2024-25, the German manager’s first year, he set career records for goals (34) and assists (22). After a poorer last year because of injuries, he has returned in full force this season.

His good form was one of the reasons for the renewal, as Trivela learned from an anonymous source who had contact with the negotiations. But it is not the only factor.

Raphinha and his staff understood that extending the contract was the best path given the moment he is experiencing and, in particular, because he is treated by the manager and the club as an important player. This is evident in every word Flick says about the Brazilian, always showering him with praise.

‘He is playing at a spectacular level. His strengths and characteristics fit our style perfectly. He always finds spaces to attack, and we also have players who can provide the final pass. He is very focused, he is our captain and he is showing his quality, which is important for us,’ Flick said after the 6-1 win over Alaves last weekend.

The captaincy mentioned by the manager was his own choice to reward the leadership of the number 11. Raphinha has always been a reference for younger players, which built trust in the dressing room, according to Trivela.

Having a foreigner as captain of one of the biggest clubs in the world is a weighty matter, but it came naturally. The Brazilian has won over the fans and created an identification that also made a difference in the renewal. For that reason there were no obstacles and the negotiation went smoothly for both sides.

When the new contract ends, Raphinha will be 33.

He is already the fourth Brazilian with the most goals for the club, with 94, level with Ronaldinho and behind only Neymar (105) and Rivaldo (130). In the overall ranking he is already in the top 25. In the Champions League, he has just equalled Robert Lewandowski, both with 23 goals, and is surpassed only by Luis Suarez and Lionel Messi.

He is a player who is increasingly becoming a Barcelona idol and, if he maintains his individual level and adds collective trophies, could finish the season as the best in the world.

United, who host Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League's lunch-time game on Saturday, head into the game on the back of a five-match winless run at league level - their joint-longest sequence without a top-flight victory this calendar year.

Noah Okafor (abductor), who missed last weekend's loss at Bournemouth, has not trained with the team this week.

A foot issue also forced Dominic Calvert-Lewin to miss training on Thursday, although Farke is cautiously optimistic that the England international will be back today.

Although it remains to be seen if he is named in the Three Lions' squad for their Nations League games against Croatia and Spain. The squad will be announced this morning.

"But I'm not just looking ahead (about) what will be in three weeks or whatever. It's not the easiest situation at the moment especially offensive-wise (with options), but we want to stay together and fight together and also make sure that in perhaps not the best situation, we still are able to dig in and grind out a result in this important game."

Meanwhile, Farke has praised the mentality of Stach, who has come on from the bench in United's past two matches after receiving pain-killing injections.

Farke commented: "I didn't want to speak in public about exactly what his injury is, also to protect him a little bit.

"But I think before we start secret discussions or whatever, these are all high-profile athletes and they are really on the highest level. Each and every detail and small percentage can disturb them in their performances. "Anton has been playing with a broken finger, with tape around his hand.

"Obviously, the finger for outfield players is perhaps not that decisive, but it's of course not ideal. But also since a few weeks he's dealing with a broken toe. His little toe is broken and that is of course painful.

"That was the reason he was not involved in the starting line-ups in the last weeks.

"But we still don't want to miss out on Anton and we are all happy that he was willing to suffer and sacrifice himself, even just to be on the bench. Because it's the same with Joe Rodon, he's important for the whole group.

"And even if I can just bring him in for 15 or 20 minutes, it's still Anton Stach who can produce a moment of magic, perhaps with a good free-kick or corner kick."

#2046. Auxerre vs. Paris FC - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 05 Nov 2026 07:12, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 07:14

Ten places separate Auxerre and Paris FC in the Ligue 1 table ahead of Saturday's matchday 10 fixture at Stade de l'Abbe-Deschamps.

Liam Rosenior's men could theoretically finish the weekend joint-top if they secure maximum points against the side with the division's worst defensive record and Paris Saint-Germain lose to Troyes.

Rosenior faced considerable criticism after his forgettable spell at Chelsea earlier this year, but the Englishman has Paris FC flying after nine matchdays.

Les Bleus sit fourth in the division with 17 points from a possible 27, level with third-placed Lyon, one behind second-placed Lille and just three adrift of local rivals PSG.

Much of their early-season success admittedly stems from their strong form at Stade Jean-Bouin, where they remain unbeaten after collecting 13 of a possible 15 points.

However, they have struggled to replicate those performances on their travels, losing half of their four away matches, including the last two against Lorient (1-0) and Lens (2-1).

Paris have not won away since early October's 3-2 success at Marseille, and a return of just four points from 12 on the road undermines their prospects of drawing level with PSG before Luis Enrique's men face Troyes later on Saturday.

Will Still's Auxerre have made a patchy start to the campaign, compounded by their failure to keep clean sheets in eight of their nine Ligue 1 fixtures.

The 14th-placed club's only shutout came in September's 1-0 victory over Nice, but Les Ajaistes have been unable to keep opponents at bay since.

That defensive weakness leaves Still's team vulnerable, and they enter Saturday's encounter having conceded 23 league goals, three more than bottom-placed Le Havre, further underlining their difficulties.

While their 13 goals exceed the totals of all but two bottom-half clubs, Brest (16) and Strasbourg (17), this weekend's hosts leave themselves with considerable work to do by conceding far too freely.

Nonetheless, eagle-eyed observers will note that Auxerre have conceded just five goals in front of their supporters while scoring as many themselves, offering encouragement ahead of matchday 10.

Given Paris' away struggles, Les Ajaistes, who have collected seven points from 12 on home soil, will back themselves to secure maximum points against Rosenior's high-flying side.

Lamfia Dioubate was dismissed after 11 minutes of the 5-1 defeat to Strasbourg last time out, leaving Auxerre without the midfielder.

While Sekou Fofana is touch-and-go due to a groin issue, Bryan Okoh, Remy Labeau Lascary and Assane Diousse are all sidelined for the hosts.

Cameron Archer leads Auxerre's scoring charts with six goals, three more than Danny Namaso, and the Englishman will aim to build on his prolific start to the campaign.

Paris, meanwhile, could be without Ligue 1's leading scorer Lassine Sinayoko, whose eight goals surpass everyone else's tally in the competition, while his five assists underline his dual threat.

Given that Sinayoko has scored half of Les Bleus' 16 league goals, the visitors may have to rely on alternative sources; only Maxime Lopez and Pablo Pagis have also scored more than once for Rosenior's side, leaving the manager short of proven match-winners.

Apart from Sinayoko, the capital club have several other injury doubts: Adama Camara (hamstring), Luca Koleosho (muscle), Jonathan Ikone (thigh) and Nhoa Sangui (muscle) could all miss out.

Auxerre's league-worst defensive record is concerning, but conceding just five goals across four home matches suggests that Saturday's assignment may be less straightforward than the table implies.

Paris have struggled to replicate their home performances on the road, and Sinayoko's potential absence could leave Rosenior's men settling for a point.

#2043. Celtic revival or one-off resistance and is Duran the best player in Scotland?

Welcome to The Burning Questions, our new daily debate where we take one major subject in Scottish sport and tackle the three questions everyone is talking about.

Each day, our writers will offer their verdicts on the biggest issues and arguments dominating the agenda. And Celtic are back under the spotlight after Martin O’Neill’s side delivered a much-needed European victory over Besiktas.

O’Neill appeared visibly emotional at the full-time whistle after watching his team produce an inspired display, but was this the start of a genuine turnaround or simply a singular act of resistance in a difficult season?

Read more: Who says Martin O'Neill is out of touch? Besiktas win was a tactical masterclass

Then there’s Camilo Duran. Celtic’s recruitment has taken plenty of criticism, but the £5.5million Colombian continues to deliver and his latest goals have strengthened his claim to be the best player in Scottish football right now.

Read more: Who says Martin O'Neill is out of touch? Besiktas win was a tactical masterclass

And what about Europe? Despite their setbacks, Celtic’s hopes of reaching the Europa League knockout play-off round remain alive. Can O’Neill’s men build on the Besiktas win and collect enough points from their remaining four games to squeeze into the top 24?

Matthew Lindsay and Graeme Young give their answers to today’s three Burning Questions.

Matthew Lindsay: Time will tell. The 7-1 mauling of Hearts last month certainly proved to be a false dawn for the Scottish champions. Defeats against Celta Vigo and Falkirk and a draw with Dundee United followed that impressive result.

Celtic were excellent against a very good Besiktas team last night. They contained opponents who had beaten Hoffenheim and Marseille and drawn with Crystal Palace extremely well, while creating a raft of scoring chances in the final half-hour. It was a deserved victory and they should have prevailed by a more comfortable margin.

But I still fear Celtic are short of the quality they need in key areas. They desperately need a physical, defensively-minded central midfielder and I suspect their lack of strength in depth will prevent them from going on an extended winning run in the weeks ahead.

That said, I didn’t expect them to produce such an inspired display against Vincenzo Italiano’s men. The performance lifted the Celtic supporters and the players can tap into that feelgood factor going forward.

Graeme Young: I have a feeling this might still prove to be the start of a roaring second half of the season that defies convention. There was every reason to be perplexed by Celtic’s starting XI, but naming the likes of Kasper Hogh and Sebastien Tounekti allowed thrilling talents such as Camilo Duran and Callum Osmand to enter the game as if they had been fired out of a cannon.

But it would be remiss to downplay Celtic’s patterns of play, or lack thereof, in the biggest matches. Besiktas turned out to be a bit of a Turkey. It’s unlikely the better teams they face will be quite so welcoming as the fixtures continue to pile up.

Matthew Lindsay: Yes. For me, the Colombian is the form player in the country just now. His brace against Besiktas took his tally for the 2026/27 campaign to 13. Considering he has often been played out of position out wide, it is some return. He has been £5.5million very well spent indeed.

There is still an awfully long way to go before the Player of the Year awards are doled out and much can change. But if Celtic improve at home and abroad in the weeks and months ahead, and their midweek win augurs well for the future, then Duran will have even more scoring chances.

There have been a few standouts in Scottish football this term. Josh Fowler at St Johnstone is the leading marksman in the top flight, Ryan Naderi at Rangers has been inspired at times and Josh McPake has forced his way into the Scotland set-up. But the former Qarabag forward is the pick of the bunch.

Graeme Young: Yes. Rangers star defender Olwethu Makhanya looks every inch a superstar in the making, but this beautiful old game of ours is ultimately decided by the players who put the ball in the net.

Duran brings goals, versatility and an uncanny knack for making the difference in the biggest moments. His connection with the aforementioned Osmand is electric and feels like Celtic’s best shot at getting themselves firing in the right direction.

Matthew Lindsay: The Scottish champions' fine win over Besiktas moved them to within a point of the clubs occupying the knockout play-off spots in the Europa League league phase table. But going through remains a tall order.

They have three difficult away matches against Torreense, Omonia Nicosia and Royal Union Saint-Gilloise coming up in the months ahead. They will need to win on the road to progress.

Second-tier Portuguese outfit Torreense, who are up next in three weeks, showed they will not be easily overcome once again last night by beating Ararat-Armenia at home to move to six points.

If Celtic maintain the levels they hit last night, they could do it. But that is a big if. I fear their opening losses to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo may come back to haunt them.

Graeme Young: Do you know what? They might just do it.

O’Neill landed wins against Feyenoord and Utrecht, as well as a point in Bologna, during the second half of their Europa League campaign last season and looks a good bet to do something similar again.

Torreense, the Portuguese second-tier side, feels like a danger mission. Damned if you do, condemned if you don’t. Omonia doesn’t look the most challenging assignment and then it’s Marseille, who are also toiling, before Celtic finish against Union Saint-Gilloise, who may already be safely inside the top eight by the time they face the Premiership champions.

If Celtic land seven points from their final four games, it might just be enough to squeeze them into the top 24. But only just.

#2042. Hearts star admits 'I need to do better' after nightmare week

Stuart Findlay wants Hearts and himself to go into the international break on a high after a damaging double defeat this week.

The injury-ravaged Gorgie side were knocked out of the Premier Sports Cup semi-finals by Edinburgh rivals Hibernian at Barclays Hampden last Sunday.

Then on Thursday, the 31-year-old former Kilmarnock, Philadelphia Union and Oxford United centre-back headed in a late consolation goal in the 3-1 Conference League loss to Thun in Switzerland.

The deflating defeat left Wouter Vrancken’s side, who had 10 players missing through injury going into the game before Stephen Kingsley had to be replaced in the second half, with one point from nine in the competition ahead of the William Hill Premiership game against Falkirk on Sunday.

Asked what Vrancken’s message was to the team afterwards, Findlay told TNTSports: “That’s obviously a couple of tough defeats in a row for us, losing the derby, then Thursday night.

“But we’ve got a massive game again on Sunday and we need to make sure we rally together, we need to be around each other.

“We know it can be difficult times. And when it’s difficult times, that’s when we need to pull through, show our character and make sure we turn around and have a good result going into the break.

“Personally, I know I need to do better if the manager gives me another chance on Sunday. I’ll make sure I do better than what I did on Thursday and all I need to take from it is to move on with the rest of the team and make sure we put things right on Sunday when we play Falkirk.

“It wasn’t what we were hoping for, obviously. We had a game plan that we obviously didn’t stick to, the way that we wanted to do it.

“I thought, we sort of didn’t get going, personally, there was a lot of duels at was back that I should be doing a lot better to understand.

“It was a really disappointing night. It’s a night that we expected more from. So we came away very disappointed.”

#2041. Barnsley FC signing and Preston legend Daniel Johnson on leadership and ignoring 'outside noise'

In his media duties, the recent Barnsley signing, who turned 34 last month, speaks with calmness, maturity, authority and good sense.

That comes with spending eight-and-a-half seasons at a club where he became an icon in Preston North End.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

In his early years at Deepdale, the attacking midfielder showed his penchant for scoring thrilling goals - as his current club can testify. While at Preston, Johnson struck six times in eight matches against the Reds.

Later seasons saw him convert into a slightly deeper role. With that came increased team responsibility befitting his senior player status. His voice could be increasingly heard on the pitch, conducting play and marshalling his North End team-mates.

Barnsley can certainly use some of that. Aside from Cam McGeehan and Luca Connell, there is not much seniority around and the Reds will need every bit of experience they can muster if they are to pull away from danger in League One.

Johnson is now ready to go after getting his fitness up to speed since heading to Oakwell last month.

He made his debut from the bench in the final quarter of last weekend’s draw with Oxford United. It was his first competitive appearance since March when he was plying his trade for Istanbul-based Fatih Karagümrük in Turkey’s second tier.

Asked about the importance of leadership, Johnson told The Yorkshire Post: "Do you know what.. It depends on the individual, the circumstances and the situation. I'm more of a speaker on the pitch than off the pitch, really.

"You kind of understand what the situation needs at that moment.

"I've had it with many players over my career. You need someone that maybe can talk to you away from the group so you can express certain things. Or you speak in a room and everyone's there and everyone's listening. Everyone can have their say.”

Barnsley’s league position - they find themselves in the bottom four with just two wins from their opening 13 League One games - is a drama, but not yet a major crisis, just a third of the way through 2026-27.

A confidence boost over the next week would be timely. They play two cup fixtures - starting with Saturday’s FA Cup first-round tie with Aldershot - before a key league appointment at fellow strugglers Wigan Athletic and a home derby with Sheffield Wednesday.

Johnson never experienced a full-blown relegation fight in his time at Preston or his two years at Stoke City.

He did sample some tough times, though. Preston were hovering just above the relegation positions in 2020-21 when they sacked Frankie McAvoy just before Christmas 2020, while Stoke were in the drop zone with a third of the season to go in 2023-24 before pulling away from trouble.

Johnson continued: "Only we can get ourselves out of this situation because only we put ourselves in it.

"Not every season that you play is going to be pretty straightforward. There are going to be times where you have little dips during the season.

"And it's just about sticking together, really and truly. Forget about the outside noise. Because at the end of the day, it's us boys in that dressing room that's going to turn it around, regardless of what the situation may be or what it looks like elsewhere.

"Like the performance the other day, you can see everyone was digging in for each other and we were fighting together. And we had a man sent off very, very early on in the game as well."

His time at Preston saw him earn the respect of Alex Neil, a widely admired EFL manager with previous Barnsley connections.

The pair forged a strong relationship together, with Johnson afforded a new lease of life under the Scot - taking to his pressing style instantly.

It augurs well for life under Stendel, who is a hands-on, demanding manager like Neil.

If Barnsley are to turn things around, you sense Johnson will play a significant role.

On life under Neil, who signed him for Stoke after he elected to leave Preston, Johnson continued: "I've a really good relationship with Alex.

"I've only got positive things to say about him. He helped me a lot. He was able to push my career and my playing style onto another level.

"He's a really, really good guy and really good manager."

Stendel reports no fresh injury issues for the Reds ahead of this weekend, although Ben Hamed Toure is absent due to a family bereavement.

The Barnsley boss confirmed: "He is not in Barnsley for private reasons and he cannot play on Saturday. At the moment, the human is more important than the player.”

Connor O'Riordan (shoulder) has an appointment with a specialist on Monday. Jack Shepherd (suspended) is also missing.

#2040. Pioli discusses current Milan team, relationship with Ibrahimovic, Scudetto win and Moreira

Stefano Pioli shared some more insight on his time as AC Milan head coach, including the impact of Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Rafael Leao and others.

Pioli was a guest on Sky Calcio Club after Juventus 2-0 Napoli last night, and he revisited the 2021-22 Scudetto win, discussing some of the characteristics of the players, and also drawing comparisons with some current squad members. MilanVibes relayed his words.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Firstly, the coach was asked about if he saw a bit of Rafael Leao in Diego Moreira, given the Belgian was the hero of the derby on Saturday night with one goal and two assists.

“I saw him against Sassuolo too, and he impressed me. He and Rabiot are really strong. Milan played a great match, Maignan made a great save… but with their starting eleven, they’re a really strong team. When Amorim made a few more substitutions, they struggled more.

“It took them a while to get to this point because they had players arriving, probably with some problems, and it takes time to find their rhythm and fitness.

“The results are showing. Modric also still has some important strength. Gonçalo Ramos is doing a great job for the team and is a very good player.”

The discussion about Milan inevitably brought them back to the team that won the league title in 2022. Pioli explained how the playing system was built around the characteristics of the players available, with particular attention to the defensive line and the ability to sustain aggressive football.

“A coach’s skill lies in adapting to a player’s characteristics. At AC Milan, I had players who got lost defending deep. I like that style of play, but it was the best one for those players.

“Kalulu and Tomori also allowed us to take risks. If you want to stay high up the pitch, you need to have significant intensity; anything in between doesn’t work.”

Pioli commented on Leao again, who reached the peak of his powers under the Italian, but also admitted that after the Scudetto not everything went as he would have hoped.

The Scudetto year was devastating. I’ve seen few players of that level. Then he wasn’t, and we weren’t, good. Because when you win, it’s because something special is created in the team. Paolo [Maldini], Ricky [Massara], and I weren’t good – and neither was he – at maintaining and further raising his level.

“He certainly has important qualities. The coach has to understand the players. Rafa is a good player who needs to be encouraged in a certain way.”

During the segment, the background on Roma’s interest also emerged. The Giallorossi contacted Pioli, but at that point the coach had already received an offer from Al Nassr.

“There were times when everyone called me. Even Roma, but I had just received my contract with Al Nassr and I couldn’t break my word.

“I don’t regret going to Saudi Arabia. I wanted to gain experience abroad after my years with AC Milan. The financial aspect and the opportunity to coach Cristiano Ronaldo also played a role.

“If you don’t coach him, you don’t understand how great he is. He’s a champion, obsessed with preparing to score goals. He’s very respectful.”

Pioli spoke about Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Cristiano Ronaldo, two of the biggest profiles that he has had to manage in his career to date.

“Cristiano and Zlatan have a very similar relationship: ‘You’re clear with me and I respect you, if you’re not clear with me, it’s no good.’ I’ve always based our relationship on clarity and sincerity.

“It’s clear that with Zlatan and Cristiano, if you tell them, ‘Look, you’re not playing tomorrow, or you’ll play 60 minutes tomorrow,’ and then I’ll take you off, and you do it or you don’t, it makes a difference.

“I didn’t tell Zlatan something once, but I didn’t tell him because in the rush, I think during the Covid period, we were playing every three days. At the end of the first half it was 0-0, then in 10 minutes we scored 2-3 goals, I don’t remember now…

“Anyway, I made three substitutions: I remember Zlatan, Calhanoglu, and another. So quick, but I hadn’t told Zlatan in advance… The next day [laughs]. he came to me… The good thing about Zlatan is that as soon as he gets over it, the next day it’s as if nothing had happened.”

When asked if Ibrahimovic frequently sulked, Pioli replied: “No, absolutely not. He’s great. But does he tell you? Yes, yes, and then with a tone…

“I always leave my office door open because I like to greet the players and see them. In fact, I had the office changed because I wanted it to be between the locker room and physiotherapy, which they have to go to every day anyway, so every day I greeted all the players, and they came in to see me.

“Every now and then I stopped them, but I didn’t stop them. That day, I didn’t expect Zlatan to come in. He came in and said, ‘I’ll speak today.’ You know, those chairs that move around, I danced for 2-3 minutes, but then it went away.”

Pioli also recalled his first meeting with the Swede, who arrived at Milanello at the end of January 2020 and undoubtedly played a key role in the resurgence.

“Ibrahimovic arrived at Milanello the first day. I waited for him there, and he arrived when it was dark. It was January, the end of January. I followed him in his training, but he also had a knee problem.

“He did a bit of treadmill work, then he came to my office, spoke to me a bit, and I explained to him how I wanted to use him on the pitch, technically and tactically. He said to me: ‘You’re the coach, I’m the player. You respect me, I’ll respect you.’ And that’s what happened.”

Pioli also spoke about the relationship between results and the team, explaining why it’s often more difficult for a coach to put a defeat behind him than to enjoy a victory.

“We coaches don’t enjoy victories because we immediately think about the next game. Defeat, however, stays with you. But what happened to me at Milan was incredibly emotional. Sackings, on the other hand, are difficult; you feel guilty.

“The one in Florence was even more difficult. I had returned with so much willpower and energy. I had returned with so much confidence, and it was a tough blow.”

Finally, a revelation about the possibility of becoming Italy’s coach. Pioli confirmed that he had been close to taking over the national team, but without going into details.

“I’ve touched on it, but not for very long. In our careers, we are the product of all the choices we make. Some are good, some aren’t.”

#2039. Simon Leslie: A brilliant Eastbourne Borough day for first-timers – and those who have been coming decades

That’s 14 wins from 15 games, and tomorrow we head to Dartford hoping to keep this extraordinary run going.

Saturday against Ramsgate had almost everything, although for a while it looked as though the one thing missing might be a goal. It was a fantastic, exciting game, but as the clock ticked down you started to think we might have to settle for a 0-0 draw.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Shay Harrison clearly had other ideas. Two brilliant late goals later, Priory Lane was bouncing. If that was your first visit, I hope you enjoyed the finish as much as I did.

And for plenty of people, it was their first visit. Our friends at Octopus Energy gave tickets to local customers, and seeing the queues stretching out towards the street was a wonderful sight. So many new faces coming to see what their local football club is all about. Thank you to everyone at Octopus who helped make it happen. They certainly brought the energy!

Eastbourne did its bit too, with beautiful blue skies and autumn sunshine. The Octopus Energy fan zone was up, the children were playing and there were smiling faces everywhere. It was one of those afternoons when you could look around and think, yes, this is what we want football here to feel like.

There is something special about bringing someone to non-league football for the first time. You are so close to the action, you can hear the players and feel every tackle, every near miss and every decision you are convinced the referee has got wrong. Then a late goal goes in and suddenly you are celebrating with someone you had never met two hours earlier.

I really hope those who joined us for the first time will come back. Bring your friends, bring the children and make an afternoon of it. We want this to be somewhere you feel welcome, somewhere you enjoy spending time and a club you are proud to call your own.

Before kick-off, our Spirit of Football team paraded with the first trophy they had ever won. The children were absolutely delighted, and their excitement was one of the highlights of my day. Just imagine how much that moment meant to them, showing off their trophy in front of our biggest crowd of the season. A huge congratulations to everyone involved.

We spend plenty of time talking about results, league positions and what happens next, but seeing those happy faces reminds you how much a football club can mean to people. It was lovely to see them getting their moment and enjoying every second.

Then came Tuesday night, and Eastbourne’s blue skies had given way to wind and rain. A very different evening against Stanway Rovers, but the winning continued with a single-goal victory. Sometimes you get sunshine and spectacular late drama; on other occasions you have to dig in and get the job done. The boys found a way again.

Thank you to everyone who braved the weather to cheer them on. Fourteen wins from 15 games is some going, and the players and staff deserve enormous credit for putting that run together. We remain third in the league, with plenty of football still to play and plenty to look forward to.

Tomorrow we head to sunny Dartford - hopefully the weather will take the hint - looking to make it 15 wins from 16. Our away support has been terrific, and I know the boys will hear you again.

To everyone who came on Saturday, whether you have been coming for decades or were finding your way to Priory Lane for the very first time, thank you. I hope we will see you again soon. Shay cannot promise two late goals every week, but he has certainly given you a reason to come back.

#2038. Arsenal suffer fresh injury blow as Mikel Arteta reveals "some issues" after Slavia Prague win

By Lewis Blain | 05 Nov 2026 07:21

Arsenal have suffered a potential injury setback after Ezri Konsa was forced off during their 2-1 win over Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Wednesday evening.

Mikel Arteta confirmed the England defender was substituted because of a fitness issue, having appeared to struggle with his knee during the match.

However, the Gunners have received a timely boost with William Saliba now fit and available again after recovering from a long-term back injury.

The Arsenal manager confirmed the substitution was fitness-related rather than tactical, explaining that the defender had been playing a considerable amount of football recently.

"Obviously he's playing a lot," Arteta said after the match, via the Evening Standard. "He's played so many games in the last few weeks. He had some issues, and we decided to take him off."

Konsa's fitness will now be monitored, particularly with Arsenal continuing to juggle their domestic and European commitments.

There was better news regarding William Saliba, however, with the Frenchman returning to the matchday squad after missing the start of the season with a back injury.

Before the match, Arteta confirmed that the 25-year-old had completed 45 minutes in a behind-closed-doors friendly without any setbacks, and claimed that "he feels ready to go" and "feels really comfortable."

Saliba's return could hardly have come at a better time for the Gunners, particularly with Konsa now carrying a potential injury concern.

The summer signing has hugely impressed alongside Gabriel, but having another established centre-back available means Arteta is not suddenly short of options.

There would be some risk in throwing Saliba straight back into the starting XI against Hull City on Saturday, especially after such a lengthy absence.

However, the upcoming fixture could offer a relatively favourable opportunity to gradually reintegrate the Frenchman, provided Arteta is satisfied with his fitness.

Konsa's situation will need assessing before any decisions are made, but Saliba's availability gives Arsenal some welcome defensive insurance at an important stage of the campaign.

#2037. St Mirren sick of Old Firm 'hard luck' stories as Rangers come calling

Craig McLeish does not want the Old Firm to be a “hard luck story” for St Mirren as he prepares for the visit of Rangers in the William Hill Premiership on Saturday night.

Since moving from the youth set-up to become Buddies boss in March – initially on a temporary basis before making the move permanent in June – McLeish’s side have run both Celtic and Rangers close on several occasions.

Most recently, St Mirren lost to a last-gasp goal in a 1-0 defeat at Ibrox, following a 2-1 home defeat to Celtic and a 5-1 defeat away to Rangers in the Premier Sports Cup.

In his dugout debut for Saints in March, Rangers won 1-0 in Paisley, before St Mirren went down 1-0 at Celtic Park before taking the Hoops to extra-time in the Scottish Cup semi-final, only to eventually lose 6-2.

McLeish said: “We don’t want to be the hard luck story every time we play against them and you get plaudits like, ‘oh well done you played well but unlucky again’.

“We want to be able to go toe-to-toe with anyone in the league and come out with positive results and against Rangers and Celtic, we have not managed to do that.

“A couple of the games have got away from us and that’s what you’re trying to fight against and make sure that the games do go right to the end and you’re always in with a chance.

“That’s the bit now for us as a group and confidence within the group, to go and get a positive result against one of them – that’s probably the next step for us.

“We’ve had a look at Rangers twice (this season) as well, and we obviously have to change some bits just because of personnel available to us.

“You’re just trying to constantly learn and adapt from the games that you’re playing against teams.

“You have to take those experiences on and just tweak little bits to it, so there will be little bits that we try and throw at Rangers that they’ve not seen from us before as well.

“That’s what we have to try to do. We have to try and be unpredictable with it.”

#2036. Hull City's Brooke Norton-Cuffy on learning life's lessons from Rotherham United to Genoa

The 22-year-old came through the Gunners' academy but his first senior match at Ashburton Grove could be in the black and amber of Hull City on Saturday.

Only could, because his education has often featured harsh lessons.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

En route to East Yorkshire were loans at Lincoln City, Rotherham United, Coventry City, Millwall, then a permanent move to Serie A Genoa.

It tested his hunger and taught him skills he can use now as he looks to oust club captain Lewie Coyle or fan favourite Ryan Giles from one of the full-back positions.

At Rotherham in the 2022-23 Championship survival was the overarching aim, just as it is for Hull in the Premier League now.

"I went from Rotherham struggling against relegation to the play-off final, so it was a funny season," says Norton-Cuffy, who did so well at the New York Stadium that Coventry stole him away mid-season.

"Rotherham wasn't the prettiest football but it was not conceding, digging deep, a test of character. It's really cold, the training pitches weren't great, they were getting waterlogged sometimes.

"It was the same on the pitch, you had to dig deep and grind out the 1-0s. On the ball, I felt the wing-backs were just isolated.

"I learned off the ball to be in a unit, really dig deep and suffer for a little bit, and on the ball try and create something and be a maverick.

"At Lincoln, I struggled for the first two weeks. I went from academy to men's football. I got a T-shirt and shorts in the middle of December. I asked the kit man for a thermal, he's gone, 'You're not at Arsenal now!'

"I struggled with the pace and intensity so I started doing extra gym sessions, extra with the coaches after training, little things.

"Then when I got my first start, it just kind of flourished."

Maybe that was what made Norton-Cuffy so fearless when his first permanent transfer took him to Genoa in 2024.

Since the Heysel ban was lifted, British footballers abroad have been rare, but there seems to be a growing willingness for the current generation to look overseas for first-team football.

"I feel like when I speak to some of my friends they don't want to go abroad whatsoever. I've never really seen it as going abroad, just playing football," argues Norton-Cuffy.

"It's not like it's 10, 12 hours to get back to my family, it's a two-hour plane journey. It's like living in Hull now – you have to drive four hours.

"You see a lot of boys playing under-21s for top academies and they struggle because they might go to a National League or League Two side not used to playing football and when you don't have a good loan, you have to drop down a level again.

"I think (overseas) clubs are realising the talent in England. There's a lot of boys who played in academies with me who could play in certain teams in Serie A and flourish."

If stereotypes about English footballers abroad are fraying, an important Serie A one remains strong.

"Tactically, defensively, staying switched on, Italy is known for being one of the best defensive leagues in the world and you really do see that in training," he argues.

"After my first year, I was getting doubled and tripled up on a lot, so it was how do I work out that, how do I still be a threat?"

Ask what is different about the Premier League compared to Serie A, and the words he reaches for are tempo, pace and intensity. He could mean life in general.

"I'm from London,” he says. “London's hectic. Hull's more like Genoa, it's more laid back, people will sit down and have a chat with you.

"When I first went over there, there was a bit of a culture shock. I'm going into a supermarket and I got an old granny speaking to the cashier for 25 minutes and I'm standing behind her waiting.

"At first I was fuming but it happened again and again. You learn to just relax a little bit and enjoy life."

If Hull is more chilled as a city, their football cannot be in the Premier League. Like so many of the Tigers' new signings, Norton-Cuffy has had to adapt.

"It's a different intensity," he argues. "And it's the stuff that people don't really see, like staying in a hotel, trying to find a house, trying to move your stuff from abroad.

"I feel settled now, I feel I'm fit, I'm in a good position to really kick on."

The right-footer's full debut came playing left-back at Fulham in Hull's worst performance of the season.

"The team played badly, I played badly, but it was a good moment for me," he says. "A learning moment."

Hidemasa Morita's groin/adductor issue makes him a doubt, but otherwise Hull pick from the same squad.

#2035. Two defeats won’t put Hastings United off-course – Dolan has strong belief in squad

United lost 1-0 in both Saturday’s clash with high-flying Faversham and Tuesday’s against lower-placed Deal Town.

The lack of points has seen them slip to fourth place, but they’re only two points behind leaders Whistable as they try to recover with tomorrow’s trip to Cray Valley PM.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Dolan was disappointed with the losses but is not about to rip up his blueprint and start again.

Faversham won with a 30th minute spot-kick and United skipper Tom Chalmers was sent off in the final moments for two yellow cards.

Dolan said: “The Faversham game was a case of us giving them a little bit too much respect. They are a good team – well-organised – and are going to be there or thereabouts this season. And you can see why they are title favourites – they’ve got great experience and some great players for this level.

"But I think we turned up giving them too much respect from the get-go and that carried on through the whole game and we didn’t really test them like I know we could have done, or how we have tested other teams this season.

"That’s disappointing from us but we’ve been fantastic up until now so I’m not going to grumble after we’ve played a team who are near the top of the league and are favourites to win it.

"We were still in the game until the very end so we’re staying in games and not getting rolled over which is good. It’s one of those where you have to dust yourselves off and move on."

On Chalmers' red card, Dolan said: “I don’t really understand what he got the first yellow for. He was talking to the ref and the ref chucked a yellow out when they were wasting time. If your captain can’t talk to the ref, then who can?

"The second yellow I think was just frustration boiling over from him at the very end. He’ll be suspended on Saturday so we’ll make do without him.

"The Deal was game was very frustrating. As I said before that game, the league table doesn’t do them justice. They’re in a false position in my eyes – like Cray Valley, who we face on Saturday.

"Deal are a good team who have been at the level for a long time and have players who have been together a while. They’re very organised and they did a job on us – they had one shot on target in the 85th minute and it happened to be a goal. Whether we put that down to a lapse in concentration, or down to moments … this game was more down to fine margins.

"We had four or five really good attempts at goal but we need to be putting these chances away. It’s good we’re still creating chances but bad we’re not taking them. I’m positive over the fact we’re still creating them.

"Against Faversham we didn’t create much but against Faversham we created some good openings – we hit the post, had a one-on-one, their keeper made a great save and there were a couple of other chances. I’m happy we’re still creating."

Dolan is disappointed but not overly alarmed at the past two results.

"Our home form has taken a dip. In the FA Trophy game conditions played a part and in that game – like the Faversham – we gave them too much respect. And in the Deal game we dominated for 80 minutes then conceded a goal,” he said.

"Up until the Faversham game we’d scored in every game so I don’t put it down to anything in particular – it’s one of those things that happens in any football season.

"You’re not going to go along winning every game or scoring in every one, but I’m still positive and upbeat about what we’re doing. I’m fine with the team and the squad and everything we’re doing and how the boys are listening to what we want.

"Anyone who has consistency will do well – look at Whitstable with eight or so wins on the bounce and now they’re top.

"We’re a very young squad – and a new squad this season – so bits of naivety will set in and learning will be a part of it and it’s down to us to help each other through it, and pick out the moments where can do better it and rectify it."

The chance to do so comes at Cray Valley PM tomorrow. They sit 20th going into the weekend.

"The Cray Valley game is another against a team I think are in a false league position. On paper it looks a perfect chance for us to go and get back to winning ways, and I’d love nothing more than for us to go and win. But I also there’s players in their team who can hurt us if we’re not on our game,” Dolan said.

"There are some real threats in their team so we have to be at it from the beginning. We won’t take them lightly. Me, Sam (Adams) and Trevor (McCreadie) have discussed threats that they have and we’ll have reiterated that to the players and have a plan in place to try to go out and win the game. We have to be at our best and I’m sure if we are, we will win.”

#2034. Derek McInnes delivers 'unbelievable' verdict on unsung Rangers standout

Derek McInnes is happy for goalkeeper Ivor Pandur to stay under the radar at Rangers.

Along with centre-back Owelthu Makhanya, the 26-year-old Croatian goalkeeper has been the Light Blues’ most consistent player this season following his move from Hull City on a four-year deal in the summer.

Pandur has brought a sense of calm to the Gers defence, which was demonstrated again in the 1-0 Premier Sports Cup semi-final win over Aberdeen at Barclays Hampden on Saturday.

Ahead of the William Hill Premiership clash with St Mirren in Paisley on Saturday night, an appreciative McInnes said: “I think he’s done so well.

“The fact I don’t really get asked a lot about Pandur, he’s just so quietly effective, and I think the players hold such a high regard for him and take confidence from him.

“There’s nothing worse — I’ve been there as a player when you’re not sure about your goalie and it affects a lot of what’s happening on the pitch. But when you know you’ve got a good one there, it sends out the exact opposite.

“The confidence that he sends throughout the team I think is clear, whether it’s dealing with things at his feet, in the air.

“His shot-stopping is unbelievable. I watch him in training – every shot has the same importance. He just wants to keep the ball out of his net and, for me, they’re the best types.

“He doesn’t try harder for one shot than he does the next one. Everything is ‘You’re not beating me’, I think he plays the game that way. He’s been brilliant.”

Rangers will face Hibernian in the Premier Sports Cup final next month and McInnes stressed the positives of taking the penultimate step towards the first trophy of the season and of his career as Gers boss.

The former Rangers midfielder said: “It’s been really as you’d expect. I think you’ve got to take the good for the game.

“It’s not easy getting to a cup final, and the fact that we’re there now, you’ve got to try and be pleased with that.

“I think the whole club — I was at the Charity Foundation ball on Sunday — and everybody’s so excited about going to the cup final, and that’s where we should be.

“It should be the norm that we should be feeling that we’re turning up at cup finals and putting ourselves in a position.

“We’ll look forward to it when it comes around, but I think it’s important now that we just really focus on this game before we get into the break, because it can easily dissipate, all that excitement and optimism, on the back of the next result.

“That’s how fickle it is. You’ve got to stay on the job.”

#2033. Enzo Maresca now doubles down on his Gianluigi Donnarumma stance after latest Man City "mistake"

By Lewis Blain | 05 Nov 2026 07:47

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has defended Gianluigi Donnarumma once again following another costly mistake during their 3-2 win over RB Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday evening.

The Italian goalkeeper was criticised after allowing Ridle Baku's effort to beat him at the near post, adding to a growing list of errors this season.

However, Maresca has shown little indication that he intends to reconsider his first-choice goalkeeper ahead of Saturday's trip to face Nottingham Forest at the City Ground in the Premier League.

Donnarumma came under scrutiny after City's latest Champions League victory, having been unable to prevent Baku from equalising shortly after half-time.

The mistake followed previous errors against Aston Villa and Paris Saint-Germain, raising questions about the 27-year-old's consistency since arriving at the Etihad Stadium.

However, Maresca insisted that the incident was not a major concern, highlighting the goalkeeper's ability to produce important saves at the other end.

"It's not a concern, but it's a mistake," the City manager told reporters, via the BBC. "He recognises, he knows that it's a mistake. And now, in 48 hours, we have Nottingham Forest away, and we need to be focused on that."

Maresca was also asked whether the upcoming international break could provide an opportunity to reconsider his goalkeeping options, but again defended Donnarumma.

"I'm not thinking about the goalkeeper situation," he said. "We're talking about a mistake, but a few minutes before, he's done a save that any keeper in the world, they're not going to do that save!"

The City boss added that Donnarumma knows his performance was "not good" enough but believes he will improve in the coming weeks.

Donnarumma's recent errors are becoming difficult to ignore, particularly given his struggles with distribution and dealing with crosses into the penalty area.

However, Maresca's options behind the Italian are not particularly convincing, making a change difficult to justify.

City allowed James Trafford to leave during the summer, despite the Englishman's potential, and arguably made their own situation more complicated by not retaining a capable alternative.

Geronimo Rulli remains the back-up, and despite penalty heroics against Brighton & Hove Albion in the Carabao Cup, Maresca has already made clear that Donnarumma is his undisputed first choice.

The Italian's shot-stopping ability is also a major asset, as demonstrated by several outstanding interventions this season.

Despite the mistakes, it is difficult to envisage Maresca dropping Donnarumma anytime soon. The 6 foot 5 shot-stopper needs to improve his consistency, but City may have to persist with him given their current alternatives.

#2032. GdS: From a curse to a blessing – the factors behind Milan’s recent derby dominance

AC Milan won the derby again on Saturday night, continuing their recent dominance of the fixture, despite Inter celebrating more silverware.

La Gazzetta dello Sport write that Milan planted their flag in the middle of the Duomo and have not removed it for two years. Something strange is happening in the city, frankly inexplicable: Inter haven’t won in eight derbies, even though on paper they’re almost always the stronger team.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Since September 2024, the Nerazzurri have had eight matches against Milan, losing six and drawing too. But why does this keep happening? The paper have attempted to offer some explanations.

Between January 2023 and April 2024, Inter won six consecutive derbies. It became Stefano Pioli’s curse. Three matches were more difficult than the others: the two 2023 Champions League semi-finals and the April 2024 derby, in which Simone Inzaghi’s side sealed the Scudetto.

It was the pinnacle for Inter fans and the worst nightmare for Milan fans, not coincidentally commemorated last night by the Nord with its choreography. From that moment on, Milan turned things around.

In September 2024, they won with Matteo Gabbia’s 89th-minute header, and it all changed from there. A pair of draws, then the 3-0 Coppa Italia win with a Luka Jovic brace, the two 1-0 wins last season (Pulisic in the first leg, Estupinan in the return), and this 3-1 win most recently.

For the reasons, you should consult a psychologist, but some things can be understood. Milan certainly play much more freely than during those terrible 15 months.

They’re definitely finding tactical solutions they didn’t have in that run under Pioli, where they pressed hard and ended up only allowing counter-attacks. They especially struggled greatly against Dimarco, Calhanoglu, and Mkhitaryan.

Paulo Fonseca initiated the change, reinforced by Sergio Conceiçao in the Supercoppa Italiana final, by Massimiliano Allegri, and now by Amorim. Milan are increasingly confident and, as much as possible in a crazy situation like the derby, control the games.

This time, they struggled very little, even in the second half, as if they had the password to counter Inter’s moves. Much of it was a question of energy: Milan no longer fear their cousins, they go head-to-head, and often win the duels in recent derbies.

Then, of course, there are the individuals. Christian Pulisic is becoming a ghost for Inter, fitting of these times. CP11 has scored in four of the last eight derbies, and they’ve all been crucial goals. With his intelligence, he understands where to strike Inter. With his speed, he surprises them.

As for that intelligence thing, Luka Modric is second to none. In the derby that Pervis Estupinan won, he was the best on the field. In Saturday’s resounding win, he helped the team manage the tempo, defended up front, winning back valuable balls, and even left the free kick to Moreira.

Add Adrien Rabiot to the list of Inter nightmares: ‘the Duke’ has earned 7.5, 7, and 7.5 again in the three Milan derbies he has played (Gazzetta ratings). Throwing all that together, and you get a one-sided fixture.

#2031. SPFL star targets goal rush after finally breaking his Premiership duck

Joel Cotterill is determined to add to his goal tally at St Johnstone after breaking his scoring duck for the Perth side last weekend.

The 22-year-old attacking midfielder, who signed for Simo Valakari’s side from Swansea City in September, notched a dramatic leveller on his eighth appearance as the 10-men Perth side fought out a 2-2 William Hill Premiership draw with Kilmarnock at Rugby Park.

Ahead of Saturday’s visit from Dundee, for whom Cotterill played on loan last season, the former Wales Under-21 player said: “It’s something that I want to build on massively. There’s no better feeling than getting it in that kind of game as well.

“That weekend is a good stepping stone for me now to just carry on and get as many as I can.”

St Johnstone have had four draws in the last six games to sit in seventh place, and Cotterill knows the next step is obvious and important. He said: “If you look at the games where we’ve had draws, we’ve been very unlucky. We had a sending off last weekend.

"I think it’s going to be a really good test for both teams.”

#2029. Heartbreak for 10 men Roffey: Roffey 1 – 2 East Grinstead

Roffey welcomed East Grinstead to the Fusion Aviation stadium for this clash between two of the Premier’s promotion chasers. The night started so well for the Boars but ended in disappointment after Callum Chesworth was controversially sent off, leaving them to play seventy minutes with ten men.

After three minutes a Luke Harrison throw in found Jordan Mase in the penalty area. The Boars skipper found Chesworth who cut the ball back for Callum Kilkenny to sweep the ball inside the far post for an early lead. Roffey were quickly into their passing rhythm, breaking up Grinstead attacks and playing their way up the field confidently. After seven minutes a short corner routine ended Byron Napper’s shot being blocked for another corner as the visitors were pushed back.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Grinstead came close on eleven minutes when Kieron Pamment got down the left and fired a shot across goal just missing the far post. Ex Hornet Charlie Harris attempted a ‘Diego Gomez’ long shot when he saw Monty Watson-Price, deputising for Charlie Burton who was playing for Bromley in the FA Youth Cup, off his line. His effort however cleared the bar. At the other end, a free kick was worked to Bailey Moyo who got past his marker, but his cross could only find Harry Howes in the Wasps’ goal.

Roffey’s high press was keeping Grinstead in most of the time but Watson Price had to be quick out of his area to block Pamment’s run when he had been beaten the offside. Grinstead regained possession and the ball was played into the area where Napper, under pressure from Dan Cole, deflected the ball over Watson-Price and into the net. The Wasp’s joy was short lived as the linesman decided that Cole was offside when the ball was played into the box.

Then came the key moment in the game. Chesworth turned away from his marker but the ball ran away from him and he put in a challenge to win it back which he appeared to have done but in doing so made contact with an opponent and the referee blew for the kick, told the Roffey striker that it was never a red card and took out his yellow. Then for some reason he changed his mind and to the surprise of most people in the ground, showed a red card.

So, with seventy minutes left, Roffey had to face one of the best teams in the league with a man less. How would they adapt? The answer was soon apparent, they continued in virtually the same manner with Mase and others getting forward to fill the gap that Chesworth’s departure had left. They continued they’re passing game, but Grinstead now had added momentum and Jack Meeres blocked a shot for a corner which after a couple of headers, ended up in Watson-Price’s arms. The Roffey stopper then had to go down sharply to his left to keep out a shot from Starkey with Meeres tidying up the rebound.

As half time approached Roffey continued to have the most possession, Mase and Gibson had shots blocked and after a long spell of possession around the Wasp’s penalty area, Howes saved Pat Gibbs drive. Watson-Price comfortably took a shot from Harris. Roffey were still getting forward earning corners and putting pressure on the visitors and when Grinstead threatened through Pamment and Cascoe Rogers, Meeres and Gibbs repelled everything coming into the box. Half time arrived with the balance of the game the same as when it had been 11v11.

Roffey started the second half with the same ten and showed no sign of sitting back and holding on. Callum Kilkenny was replaced by Evan Hoarty on fifty minutes after a knock but this made no difference to the Boars approach. Gibbs headed away when Perry looked like he was going into get onto a cross 8 yards out.

Roffey were getting forward in numbers and when Mase got to the byline and pulled the ball back, it was right back, Luke Harrison he found, unfortunately Harrison’s shot missed the far post by inches. Mase again got behind the defence, this time finding Moyo whose shot could not beat Howes. A third chance to get the important second goal came when Hoarty weaved his way into a shooting position but could not get the contact he would have wanted with the shot which was again saved by Howes.

As often seems to happen a missed chance at one end is followed by a goal at the other. Cooper headed wide from a corner then for the first time Pamment found some space in the Boars defence and finished clinically for the equaliser. Tom Caplin came on for Bailey Moyo and as we entered the last ten minutes, Teddy Wood, who had covered every blade of 3G grass was replaced by Max Mesquita. Both teams were still in the hunt for the three points with Omar Folkes adding to the Grinstead forward line but as we entered stoppage time, maybe fatigue finally got the Boars who couldn’t clear a corner and after a scramble it was Folkes who managed to force it home. Cue wild celebrations from the visitors and their bench.

Roffey pinned Grinstead in their half for the last three minutes but couldn’t find the final touch to get an equaliser. They did get the ball in the net but it was ruled out for offside. It had been great effort with ten men for most of the game but looking back the Boars will know they had created the chances to win the game. Small margins count in the end and although they received great compliments from the opposition and their supporters the young Boars were left with a feeling of frustration. They will have a chance to get back on the winning trail on Saturday at Little Common.

Roffey: Watson-Price, Harrison, Gibson, Napper, Gibbs, Meeres, Wood(Mesquita), Mase, Chesworth, Kilkenny(Hoarty), Moyo(Caplin) Subs: Allen, Berry.
